sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 45561 of 2024
Applicant :- Pratap Singh Raghav

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Shikhar Awasthi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Heard Sri Shikhar Awasthi, learned counsel for the applicant and Dr. S. B. Maurya, learned AGA-I for the State-respondent.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
218 of 2023, under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 471, 342, 506 & 120-B IPC, Police Station Jewar,
District Greater Noida (Commissionerate Gautam Budh Nagar), during pendency of the trial in the court below.

entities.text:
Police Station Jewar,
District Greater Noida (Commissionerate Gautam Budh Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that on the basis of false allegations applicant has been made accused in the present matter alongwith ten others including co-accused Manish Jadaun and after considering entire facts of the case, co-accused Manish Jadaun has been released on bail by this Court and his bail order has been annexed as annexure-9 to the affidavit.

4. He further submitted that case of applicant is on better footing than Manish Jadaun as admittedly neither there is any allegation that he either received any money or any money was transferred in Pratap Singh Raghav vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99280659/
1 his account.

entities.text: Pratap Singh Raghav vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. He further submitted that however apart from the present case applicant is having criminal history of six other cases but criminal history of the applicant has been explained in the instant bail application.

6. He further submitted that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate and in the present matter, applicant is in jail since 4.10.2024.
7.
Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the arguments on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Considering the fact that co-accused Manish Jaudaun has already been released on bail by this Court and case of applicant is on better footing than him and criminal history of the applicant has been explained in the instant bail application and all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate and in the present matter, applicant is in jail since October, 2024, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant-Pratap Singh Raghav, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
12. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

13. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 12.12.2024 Ankita  Pratap Singh Raghav vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99280659/
